title: The House of the Virtuous
english: "It shall be to you like the all-herb of the field." For he was not dividing [life] as one who is thus devastated and ageless produces offspring; for this one was devouring worms and slugs. And what did he mean by 'the lifestyle of a tent'—is he not complaining about not having a tent at all, but having thrown it away?

Therefore, since the history is being drawn toward sensible things, the mind must be guided wisely, especially since we thought those who went before were not unsuitable for the kind of teaching; for they do not seem trivial. For on account of ignorance, Job is urged to bring a sacrifice to God for their sins (Job 42:8), and indeed even friends (Job 42:8-12) of such greatness (Job 42:8-12) and virtue (Job 42:8-12) follow (Job 42:8-12); to know that one cause of the inductions exists, they were struck.

It is therefore said that: of the 'wild beasts,' as it was given that they 'would be at peace with you,' and the 'house' of your mind 'will be at peace,' and 'the lifestyle of your tent,' which is the improvement in your progress, 'will not complain.' And in addition to these, 'you will know' that in your good thoughts a 'seed' multiplies, resulting in the generation of children and becoming real. Like 'the all-herb of the field,' growing through the spark of virtue and increasing even more.

And indeed, we find 'house' used by the saints in the divine writings to mean a disposition, a way of life, a virtue, just as it is written concerning the midwives of the Hebrews: "because the midwives feared God, they made houses for themselves" (Exodus 1:17), which shows the virtue constructed by them from the fear of God. For they were not without dwellings before this. And what is said in Proverbs: 'The houses of transgressors will require cleansing, but the houses of the righteous are acceptable' (Proverbs 15:25). For this is said not of sensible things but of the dispositions in the mind — the base ones needing cleansing, the virtuous ones proving acceptable; 'acceptable' meaning not 'choiceworthy to someone' but 'worthy of praise.' For the good is choiceworthy even if no one chooses it, and acceptable even if no one accepts it.
It is not something chosen by a person, but something worthy of praise; for the good is something chosen even if no one chooses it. Chooses it, and it is acceptable even if no one accepts it.

And regarding the saying about 'the one fearing the Lord and desiring his commandments exceedingly' (Ps 112:3): 'wealth and glory in his house' is not spoken concerning a sensible house or glory; for many fearing God do not have either human glory or a wealthy house, like Elijah, like Elisha and those similar. Of the 'one being rich in good works' and 'in every word and in all knowledge' (1 Tim 6:18), as Paul writes, [he is] having wealth and glory in the house of the intellect and being adorned through all virtues in his way of life.

Furthermore, the Gospel clarifies such a house; for it says: 'whoever hears my words and does them is like a prudent man, who built his house upon the rock, and the rain descended, the winds blew, the rivers came, and the house was not shaken' (Matt 7:24-25), which is the state of the virtuous person of having turned the words of the Lord into works, who remains without want, not being harmed by any of the opposing energies. For upon 'the rock' [he has] 'Christ,' the one of such a kind has established his state and his choice. For to the one confessing him, it was said by him: 'You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church' (Matt 16:18); but to the one hearing the words as they happen and not connecting deeds to the words, [he is] 'a foolish man resembling one who built his house upon the sand' (Matt 7:26), which is the state upon the fluid things of life, things not receiving firm foundations.

Therefore, this one being unstable, he has a quick fall after a short trial being sent, whether through teaching from another or through some circumstance being led by an evil spirit. He who has a stable standing of the praiseworthy house will, according to Moses, be heard toward God. 'But you...'
